Rules / Modernization

SK1013 Use a list pattern for guarded element checks

Null, fixed-length and constant element checks on an array or string can be combined into a list pattern.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 11.0
Since1.3

Why

A list pattern states the shape being tested without repeating the receiver and indices. Requiring a stable receiver, an explicit null guard, a proven exact length, and side-effect-free built-in element comparisons keeps the rewrite local. Untested positions become discards, not slices or allocations.

Example

Instead of:

bool M(int[]? a) => a != null && a.Length == 2 && a[0] == 1 && a[1] == 2;

Write:

bool M(int[]? a) => a is [1, 2];

When it does not fire

Only one-dimensional zero-based arrays and strings of checked lengths 1 through 8 are supported, with at least one constant-index equality. The null guard must precede the length check and the element tests; a combined Length property pattern from SK1011 is also accepted. Indices must be distinct and in range, and element types/constants must have built-in integral, bool, enum or string equality. Custom indexers, floating-point values, captured/ref receivers, directives, comments, expression trees, caller-argument-expression capture and ambiguous pattern identifiers are excluded. Constant dependencies must come from metadata or this source file, including transitive initializers. Concurrent unsynchronized mutation of the input is not supported.
